metadata.geometry_method: Overpass corridor fetch per branch (all railway ways: rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled), Dijkstra over a graph in which ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q cost 1x and everything else 3x, waypoints taken from the research report's own via lists and snapped by a dynamic program over up to eight candidate nodes each, with each leg confined to a corridor around its own straight line so the router cannot wander onto a parallel railroad. Every feature's geometry_quality gives its traced length against the report's documented mileage and names any straight-line legs.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: EVERY BRANCH IN THIS FILE THAT ENDS IN 1952 HAS AN UNKNOWN, WITHHELD END YEAR. The Feb 1952 Official Guide is a single snapshot: it proves the trains were running in September 1951 and says nothing about when they stopped. The Burlington's branch passenger service was swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and NOT ONE of those discontinuances has been dated by any source consulted. A 1952 end here is where the evidence stops, not where the trains stopped -- do not 'fix' one by rounding it up. Nor is a start year the year a line opened: it is the earliest year a timetable proves, usually a branchline.uk Official-Guide snapshot letter (1875, 1884 or 1893), and the lines are older than the map shows. branchline.uk cannot close a Burlington branch, only open one: outside Nebraska's single d = 1950t there is NO lettered timetable snapshot for the CB&Q between 1893 and 1976 in any of Fowler's state files, and the Missouri CB&Q legend is blank in every position. Still unexploited, and the highest-value source left for this railroad: the 1952 Guide's index of stations carries a per-station freight-only dagger across the whole 11,000-mile system, but the OCR has mangled that dagger into at least four different characters and it was not used.

properties.line: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Chariton – Blythedale
properties.speed_source: estimated, NOT sourced: a secondary branch of this era, taken from the kind of service the Feb 1952 Guide shows (Table 17) rather than from any timetable's running times
properties.geometry_quality: Real trace from OpenStreetMap: a Dijkstra shortest path over every railway way (rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled) in a corridor around the route, with ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q costed at 1x and all other track at 3x, so the path stays on the Burlington's own alignment wherever OSM records it. Snapped to the report's own station list; every one of the 5 waypoints lies within 3.4 km of the drawn line. OSM lines followed: Chicago Burlington & Quincy (abnd) 32 mi; [abandoned] 21 mi; Cinder Path 10 mi; [rail] 0 mi; BNSF Ottumwa Subdivision 0 mi. TRACED LENGTH 60.5 mi against a DOCUMENTED 120 mi (-50%). No straight-line approximation: the whole route is on mapped track. MILEAGE NOTE: the 120 mi checked against is Chariton all the way to St. Joseph; this feature stops at Blythedale, MO because OSM carries no track on the Missouri continuation. The report's own figure for the drawn portion is "approx 60 mi to Giles, continuing west", which the traced 60 mi matches. ERA NOTE: much of the surviving alignment is today's BNSF, which is the CB&Q's own successor on this route, so the modern centreline is the historical one; where the line is abandoned the trace follows the recorded grade. Simplified to a 20 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance.

No source consulted dates when passenger service actually stopped here; the Burlington's branch trains were swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and not one of those discontinuances has been dated. The end year is a withheld unknown, not an abandonment -- DO NOT extend this line to a rounder year without evidence. Equally, 1875 is the earliest year positively CONFIRMED, not the year the line opened: the branch is older than the map shows, and the confirmed start is deliberately late rather than guessed early. DRAWN ONLY AS FAR AS BLYTHEDALE, MO. Report block [25] runs the line on to St. Joseph, but OSM carries no track within 6 km of St. Joseph on this alignment, so the Missouri continuation past Blythedale is left untraced rather than ruled in. The Giles - Mount Ayr stub, which shares Table 17, is likewise not drawn. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

properties.line: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Red Oak – Hamburg
properties.speed_source: estimated, NOT sourced: a secondary branch of this era, taken from the kind of service the Feb 1952 Guide shows (Table 49) rather than from any timetable's running times
properties.geometry_quality: Real trace from OpenStreetMap: a Dijkstra shortest path over every railway way (rail, abandoned, disused, razed, dismantled) in a corridor around the route, with ways tagged old_railway_operator=CB&Q costed at 1x and all other track at 3x, so the path stays on the Burlington's own alignment wherever OSM records it. Snapped to the report's own station list; every one of the 5 waypoints lies within 0.8 km of the drawn line. OSM lines followed: Farragut Spur 21 mi; [abandoned] 16 mi; Red Oak Industrial Track 1 mi; [dismantled] 0 mi; Monroe Street 0 mi; [rail] 0 mi. TRACED LENGTH 38.1 mi against a DOCUMENTED 39 mi (-2%). No straight-line approximation: the whole route is on mapped track. ERA NOTE: much of the surviving alignment is today's BNSF, which is the CB&Q's own successor on this route, so the modern centreline is the historical one; where the line is abandoned the trace follows the recorded grade. Simplified to a 20 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance.

segments.note: branchline.uk iowarrs route 16 (Red Oak - Hamburg): four stations lettered y = the 1875 Official Guide. Feb 1952 Table 49, times legible. THE 1952 END IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END. No source consulted dates when passenger service actually stopped here; the Burlington's branch trains were swept away somewhere between about 1952 and 1968 and not one of those discontinuances has been dated. The end year is a withheld unknown, not an abandonment -- DO NOT extend this line to a rounder year without evidence. Equally, 1875 is the earliest year positively CONFIRMED, not the year the line opened: the branch is older than the map shows, and the confirmed start is deliberately late rather than guessed early. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start year 1875 from branchline.uk (John Fowler, Passenger Stations & Stops) -- branchline.uk iowarrs route 16 (Red Oak - Hamburg): four stations lettered y = the 1875 Official Guide. End year 1952 from Table 49 of the Feb 1952 Official Guide -- Feb 1952 Table 49, times legible. The end is a FLOOR on service, not the year it stopped. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are estimates and are NOT sourced.
